title: Scalar reduction of the normal-bundle vector factor
statement: Fix the finite purity conventions [def-pur-conventions] and the actual comparisons [def-pur-finite-diagonal-reduction-comparisons]. Let f:X to Y be separated, quasi-compact, locally of finite type and smooth of pure relative dimension d over the algebraically closed base field k, with Y separated of finite type. Let A=A_E,n and B=A_E,m for 1<=m<=n, and Q be derived scalar extension. Use the source and normal sections of the diagonal and the root-line conventions [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. There exists a coefficient-line comparison e fixed by the root-power and scalar-generator normalizations, for which the vector factor v_R: C_R(pi,z) to R_X(d)[2d] satisfies q_L Q(v_A)=v_B q_N. No claim about the base-change or DNC factor is made. Identity reductions, d=0, empty schemes and arbitrary ramification are included.

proof.text:
construct the coefficient-line comparison from the root-power map, its
scalar-unit adjunct, and the rank-one root generators. Ordinary tensor balancing
identifies its tensor powers. Reduction of the ordered affine integration adjunct
follows from the supported product square and exceptional transpose compatibility.
It holds for each trivialization of the normal bundle and glues, since the
integration adjunct is intrinsic. Invert that isomorphism and restrict it to the
normal zero section. The site-comparison counit equation identifies the transported
map with normalSectionMap and the tensor-power target with proTwistMap. This proves
the displayed square for the prescribed vectorFactor, including rank zero and
arbitrary ramification; quotient flatness is never used.

theorem diagonalVectorReduction :
    ∃ e : CoefficientLineComparison (quotient P m hm hmn)
        P.diagonalExponent (P.finiteReductionSetting m hm).diagonalExponent
        P.diagonalExponent_annihilates
        (P.finiteReductionSetting m hm).diagonalExponent_annihilates X,
      (proScalar (quotient P m hm hmn) X).map (vectorFactor P d f aY).hom ≫
        proTwistMap d e =
      normalSectionMap P m hm hmn d f aY ≫
        (vectorFactor (P.finiteReductionSetting m hm) d f aY).hom
